gate0.note:
GATE 0: idea-02 Tenpin. Human decision, stated as 'Go with 2 - Tenpin'. No rationale was given beyond the choice, and none is invented here.

CARRY TO GATE 1 - the idea's own two stated risks:
  1. The perfect game and the all-gutters game are both satisfied by wrong code
     (3*frame and 0 respectively), so the spare-heavy mixed game is the
     load-bearing fixture. Criteria must pin the whole cumulative array, not the
     final total, or two errors that cancel go green.
  2. The tenth frame is three rules in one place and is where this overruns.
     It should be its own cut inside session 2, with the frame-box styling
     shipped rather than cut.

BUDGET: five consecutive projects have overrun their session cap; pipeline-test-03
session 1 measured 47 minutes against 40. This idea is 2 x 40.

gate1.note:
GATE 1 APPROVED - round 4. Human decision ("add the mutation owner then approve
gate 1"). The stopping rule was approve-eligible on its own; no --override.

RULE: 0 blocking, 4 worth a look, 0 blocking findings owned by 'nothing'.
Linter 0 errors / 0 warnings. Drift against round 3: none. verify_later empty.
Sessions 38.8 / 37.4 against the 40 cap. 12 criteria, 5 cuts, all five declaring
writes_into with hints that name it (E121 clean).

TRAJECTORY: findings 10 -> 10 -> 6 -> 4; blocking 3 -> 3 -> 1 -> 0. Rounds 1 and
2 did not converge and the reason was a pipeline defect, not the spec - see
PIPELINE CHANGES below.

VERIFIED, not taken on trust:
  - Round 3's A1 is fixed in the two places the rejection brief named: the
    cut-score-lookahead bullet now says the block applies its three arithmetic
    rules unconditionally and never tests rolls.length, pendingFrame is the only
    place the end of rolls is checked, and scoreGame pushes null for a pending
    frame; the Grading integrity paragraph now states that this is what makes
    c-2-4 and c-2-6 fail when cut-pending-frame is empty.
  - Rounds 1-3's fixes are all intact. spec.json is otherwise line-for-line
    identical to .pipeline/round-3/spec.json.
  - Round 3's five worth-a-look findings, recorded in why.md as deliberately
    kept, came back listed as adjudicated rather than re-raised. That was the
    first live test of the why.md carry-forward and it held.
  - The Breaker re-derived all four frame splits, cumulative arrays and totals
    by hand, and the session-load table reproduces exactly against lint.json.

SHIPS AS WRITTEN - all four remaining findings are owned 'nothing' and none is
blocking. Accepted with eyes open:
  B1 - which block owns the end-of-rolls guard is decided in spec.md, which the
       student never reads, while cut-score-lookahead's hint is unchanged. The
       Builder cannot guess (the spec now decides it) and mutation.py's
       leave-one-out enforces it on app/ at step 8; the residue is student-side.
       NOTE: now that `mutation` is a valid owner, a future pass would likely
       park this on mutation rather than nothing. It is non-blocking either way,
       so the gate was not re-run for it.
  B2 - the step from frameScore to the cumulative array is unwritten. Changes
       only how the open skeleton looks (empty cells vs a column of zeroes); no
       graded value moves.
  B3 - "one frame box and one score cell per entry frames() returned" is graded
       only where the answer is ten, so a padded ten-box grid passes every
       criterion and g-partial's page could ship with four empty boxes. CARRY TO
       GATE 2: this is a criterion-shaped hole, not a test-shaped one, and
       neither mutation nor skeleton-check will catch it. Read c-2-6's result
       against a real g-partial page by hand.
  B4 - the scan hint states "a 10-roll game leaves out with 6 entries", which is
       false for most 10-roll games. Wording in a hint the student reads.

PIPELINE CHANGES made between rounds 2 and 4, because rounds 1-2 were failing on
the pipeline rather than on the spec (all recorded in the working tree, selftest
394 checks green):
  1. The Spec Breaker had no memory of prior rounds while the Spec Writer did.
     It writes both fields the stopping rule reads - blocking and owner - so each
     round re-rolled the verdict on unchanged text. Measured: 4 of round 2's 10
     findings were re-raises of round-1 findings and 3 of those 4 had moved
     classification, including c-1-6 going worth-a-look -> blocking on a
     byte-identical criterion. Fixed in the workflow prompt and the skill.
  2. gate1-check now detects that drift by script, keying findings on the spec
     ids they cite rather than on their own ids (which renumber) or their quoted
     line (which gets re-worded). Informational only - it never changes a
     verdict.
  3. spec_linter E121/E122/W068: every cut declares writes_into and its hint must
     backtick that symbol. Round 2's A1 - hints saying `frames` while the
     declared accumulator was `out` - is now caught deterministically.
  4. `mutation` added to the Gate 1 owner vocabulary and to FAIL_OPEN. It was
     missing, so "the cut can be left empty with every criterion green" - the one
     class mutation.py exists to catch - had nowhere to be parked, and round 3
     was rejected with owner 'nothing' for lack of the word. A missing word cost
     a round.
  5. gp-phase1-spec.js reported ready:true on a rejected gate (hardcoded). Now
     ready: !!verdict.ok.

NOT YET COMMITTED at the moment of approval: the pipeline changes above and four
rounds of spec history. lessons.md:154 says commit the approved spec before the
code phase - do that before step 7.
